doc.title: Jimmy Heath — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: The Heath Brothers today and the big band
title: 'Big P', 'Really Big' and the big band record 'Turn Up the Heath'
summary: Heath explains that 'Big P' dates from 1960's 'Really Big', and was re-arranged on his recent big band album mixed by Mtume.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: And “Big P,” is that a composition on that album, too?
Didn’t you play that on that album, no?
I thought you played it on that album.
No, that’s on the big band record. About five years ago, four or five years ago, I made a big band recording.

Yes, and it was mixed by my son Mtume, and it’s a very good record. But on that one I played a new arrangement of “Big P”. I wrote “Big P” in 1960, when Percy was still with the MJQ and I recorded it with him on a Riverside record called, “Really Big”. I had ten pieces and I called it, “Really Big”. I had Cannonball, and Percy, and Tootie, Cedar Walton. You know, French horns, and a lot of other instruments, Nat Adderely, and Clark Terry, but that’s when “Big P” was written. This is the one that’s dedicated to Percy now. When I did the big band record, “Turn Up The Heath”, for a company who…it’s a guy named Tom Bellino that I did that for. Anyway, that happened since the nineties, I did some big band things. And incidentally, I’ve been writing some things for the Dizzy big band. I’m playing in the Dizzy Alumni Big Band, and I still have my own big band. We’re going to the Bluenote this week, Feburary 2nd of this year, Feburary 2nd of 2010. Antonio, my student, plays in the band, Jeb, David Wong, Louis Nash on drums. Tootie doesn’t like to play big band music.
